scenes.title: NVG Driving: Do's & Don'ts
scenes.text: Night vision driving: do's and don'ts. This simulation covers operating the M1075A1 Palletized Load System truck while wearing the AN/PVS-14 monocular night vision device, under the Army Driver and Operator Standardization Program, AR 600-55.

scenes.title: AR 600-55: NVD Driver Requirements
scenes.text: AR 600-55 sets the rules. Before you drive under night vision devices, you must already be licensed on the M1075A1. You then complete NVD driver training: academic instruction, hands-on device training, and a supervised night practical, following TC 21-305-2. Once you pass, the NVD qualification is recorded on your operator license record, DA Form 5984-E. Stay current through your unit's sustainment program.

scenes.title: Drive Unqualified
scenes.text: Don't drive under NVDs if the qualification is not on your license record. Being licensed on the PLS in daylight is not the same as being qualified to drive it on goggles. No annotation, no NVD driving.

scenes.title: PMCS the PVS-14
scenes.text: Do perform PMCS on the PVS-14 before every mission. Check the battery, and carry a spare. Inspect the lenses for cracks, scratches, and dirt. Confirm the mount locks securely and the device sits stable on your helmet. Watch for the low battery indicator in the eyepiece.

scenes.title: Focus Correctly
scenes.text: Do focus the device correctly. First, set the eyepiece diopter until the image noise is sharp. Then adjust the objective focus at a distance, out past the front bumper, where you need to see the road. A poorly focused tube dramatically cuts your detection range.

scenes.title: Drive as a Crew
scenes.text: Do drive as a crew. Your assistant driver or vehicle commander should also be wearing NVDs, calling out hazards, and watching the right side of a ten-wheel truck that is longer and wider than your goggles make it feel. Brief the route, the hazards, and the risk assessment before you roll.

scenes.title: Use White Light in the Cab
scenes.text: Don't use white light in the cab. A flashlight, a phone screen, or bright dash lighting will wash out the image, and destroy the dark adaptation of your unaided eye. Dim the instrument panel, and use only NVG-compatible or filtered light when the crew needs to read.

scenes.title: Scan Constantly
scenes.text: Do keep your head moving. The PVS-14 gives you only a forty-degree field of view, a narrow tube compared to normal vision. Scan left, center, and right, and check both mirrors with your unaided eye. Objects outside the circle simply do not exist to you until you look.

scenes.title: Overdrive Your Goggles
scenes.text: Don't overdrive your goggles. The PLS is a heavy truck, and its stopping distance grows quickly with speed. If you can only detect a hazard at the edge of your NVD range, your speed must let you stop well inside that distance. Reduce speed for dust, rain, low illumination, and rough terrain.

scenes.title: Stare Into Bright Lights
scenes.text: Don't stare into bright light sources. Headlights, fires, and illumination rounds cause blooming and halos that hide everything around them. Look away from the source, keep the truck in your lane, and slow down until the device recovers.

scenes.title: Keep Your Interval
scenes.text: Do maintain increased intervals in convoy. Depth perception is poor through a monocular, so closing speed is hard to judge. Use the infrared markers on the vehicle ahead, keep the interval set in the convoy brief, and never tailgate.

scenes.title: Back Without a Ground Guide
scenes.text: Don't back the PLS without a ground guide, day or night. At night, the ground guide uses infrared chemlights or wands that the driver can see through the PVS-14. If you lose sight of the ground guide, stop immediately.

scenes.title: Manage Fatigue
scenes.text: Do manage fatigue. NVD driving is mentally and visually demanding. Follow your unit's driver rest plan, rotate drivers when allowed, and speak up if you are too tired to drive safely.

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.text: To recap. Do: be NVD qualified per AR 600-55, PMCS and focus the PVS-14, drive as a crew, scan constantly, keep your intervals, and manage fatigue. Don't: drive unqualified, use white light, overdrive your goggles, stare into lights, or back without a ground guide.

scenes.title: Drive to Standard
scenes.text: Train as you fight, and drive to standard. Verify all procedures against the current AR 600-55, TC 21-305-2, the vehicle technical manual, and your unit SOP.
